title: Zoho One Pricing 2026: Plans, Per-User Costs, Add-Ons
summary: Zoho One pricing runs $9-$11 per user monthly on Essentials and $90-$105 on Flexible-User, so you can decide which plan works for your budget.
body_markdown:
## Syncing Zoho One with tools outside the suite using Activepieces


When data has to move between Zoho apps and tools Zoho doesn't make, Activepieces connects them through a flow, drawing on 747 integrations counted from its open source monorepo. It fixes the plumbing between them, not the license you pay for Zoho One.


That distinction matters once you've counted the apps your team will actually open and found one or two that live outside the suite.


### Where an outside workflow tool helps


Say your sales team lives in Zoho CRM, but support runs in a help desk Zoho doesn't make. Without a connection, someone copies customer details between them by hand, and every missed copy is a customer who gets asked the same question twice.


That chore goes away with a flow in Activepieces, and flows are unlimited on every plan, including the free one. A flow is a chain of steps: something happens in one tool (the trigger), and the following steps act on it.


In the screenshot below, the builder shows a small three-step flow: a webhook trigger that catches incoming data, a code step that reshapes it, and an end. The Version History panel on the right lists two saved versions, each with a timestamp.


Take from it that you can change a flow, see what you changed, and go back if the change breaks something. That's the safety net a non-engineer needs, because a bad edit to a live sync otherwise means bad records until someone notices.


The 747 integrations in the open source monorepo are the pool a flow draws on, so a tool outside Zoho can receive the result of whatever happens in Zoho CRM.


Where no ready-made integration exists, the webhook trigger shown on the canvas lets almost any tool that can send a web request start a flow.


### Where it does not


Connecting Zoho One to Activepieces doesn't change what Zoho charges you, and Activepieces has its own free plan at $0 with 1,000 credits a month. Your plan type, whether you license employees or all users, and any add-ons are set inside Zoho.


A missing connector is the usual gap between Zoho and an outside tool, and with a closed catalogue you wait on the vendor's roadmap to fill it.


In Activepieces you can generate the missing integration with AI and add it privately to your own instance, with no release or ticket in a queue.


Roughly 60% of the 747 integrations counted in the open source monorepo came from the community, though anyone touching Zoho data still needs a Zoho seat.


So treat Activepieces, which MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run in production, as a fix for the gaps between tools, not for the invoice. Check the licensing questions with Zoho in writing before you sign.


If nearly everything you run is a Zoho app, Zoho Flow, Zoho's own automation product, is the natural alternative. Compare the two on which tools you need to reach, not on the idea that either one trims the bill.
